proposal.title: adm.counter: numbers kept as blocks, opt-in per counter
proposal.author: Giovanni Porcari

problem.p: A recycling counter (recycle=True) keeps its free numbers in the holes Bag of the counter record. The Bag is a second copy of what the document table already says, and it drifts from it: genropy/genropy#1879 shows a release that took the counter back below numbers in use, and alignSequences is needed to rebuild the state from the documents.

The goal is a model of the numbers of a series that is easy to keep consistent, gives the free numbers and their allowed dates without extra searches, and keeps the current API: counter_<field>(), assignCounterColumn, releaseCounterColumn, guessCounter.

section.title: How the counter works today
section.fact: The free numbers of a series live in the holes column (dtype X) of its adm.counter record, one node per hole with cnt_from, cnt_to, date_from, date_to.
_getCounter recycles only when the counter has a date_field: recycle = counter_pars.get('recycle') if date_field else False. Without a date the key is ignored silently.
A new number with a date earlier than last_used is refused unless date_tolerant is set.
releaseCounter reads the number back from the formatted string with int(sequence[N_start:N_end]): decimal only.
_alignOneSequence rebuilds holes and the counter from the documents; with fix_duplicate (line 157) it rewrites the number of a duplicated document by appending _.
trigger_assignCounters calls assignCounterColumn for every counter column on insert and on update, unless the record goes back to draft; it receives old_record but does not pass it on.
trigger_releaseCounters releases only recycling counters, and keeps the number on a return to draft when the counter has assignIfDraft.
assignCounterColumn and releaseCounterColumn (line 1581) are the only two points where a table calls adm.counter to assign or release.
GnrApp.experimentalValue(group, name) reads experimental.group?name from instanceconfig.xml.

section.title: Open pull requests on the same code
section.p: genropy/genropy#1881 fixes the release between numbers in use with a LIKE search on each side. genropy/genropy#1882 adds claiming a number set by hand, listing the free numbers and keeping a number on draft. Both work on the holes Bag; this proposal does not depend on them.

section.title: Blocks
section.p: The numbers of a series are a contiguous sequence of blocks, without overlaps, from the first number to the last one assigned. A block is either occupied (consecutive numbers in use) or free (consecutive numbers released). Consecutive numbers in use stay in one block: there is no row per number.
Every block carries its first and last number, and the value of order_field of its first and of its last number. For a free block these are the values of the occupied numbers that delimit it.
The idea comes from the timeline of package tmsh (gnrwork), where a resource is a sequence of contiguous holes, allocating splits a hole and releasing merges the free neighbours.

example.title: Assign 1, 2, 3, then release 2
example.code: assign 1 occupied 1-1 assign 2 occupied 1-2 assign 3 occupied 1-3 release 2 occupied 1-1 | free 2-2 | occupied 3-3
example.p: The window of the free block 2-2 goes from the last value of block 1-1 to the first value of block 3-3: both are already stored.

list.item: New number: last number of the highest occupied block plus one; the block grows, or a new occupied block starts above a free tail.
Recycled number: the lowest free number whose window holds the record's order_field value; its free block shrinks or disappears and merges with the occupied neighbours.
Number set by hand: it splits the block that holds it; refused if it is occupied or outside its window.

Release of number n: n becomes free and merges with the free neighbours. When n lies inside a longer occupied block, the new edges n-1 and n+1 need their order_field values: they are read with one equality query on the counter field, using formatSequence(n-1) and formatSequence(n+1). Releasing the last number takes the series back to the previous occupied number.
The triggers act only when the number changes: trigger_assignCounters passes old_record.
Every operation runs under the lock of the series record (for_update on adm.counter).

section.title: Counter keys

table.title: Keys of counter_<field>() in the new model

row.cell: Required when the format holds a period ($YYYY, $YY, $MM, $DD): it decides the series of the record. It no longer implies an order.

Optional. The numbers must follow the order of this field. Dtype D: dates are compared, two documents of the same day fit in any order. Dtype DH or DHZ: the full timestamp is compared. Missing: no order check.
Requires order_field; without it the configuration is an explicit error.
Not used: a counter without order_field is tolerant.

section.p: All the other keys keep their meaning: format, code, starting_value, base, assignIfDraft, showOnLoad, onAssigned, onReleased, rootstore.

section.title: Opt-in and switch of a series
section.p: The blocks live in the new table adm.counters_n, one row per block, linked to the adm.counter record of the series. The new model is opt-in through an experimental switch, read with experimentalValue('new_counters', 'counters'): * enables it for every counter, a comma-separated list of pkg.table.field for the listed ones. assignCounterColumn and releaseCounterColumn choose between adm.counter and the new model; counters not enabled behave as today.

list.item: analyzeCounter(table, field): read-only analysis of every series of the counter, with the errors not_a_number, missing_order_value, duplicate, wrong_order. No document is changed.
loadCounter(table, field): load of the blocks from the documents, for the clean series only; a series with errors is reported and skipped.
The counter is added to the switch.

section.p: checkCounter(table, field) compares the stored blocks with the documents, read-only, and replaces the checking part of alignSequences. freeSequences(table, field, record) lists the free numbers of a series with their window. The table that numbers a field is tblobj.counterTable(field) in gnrdbo; adm.counters_n implements assignCounter, releaseCounter and guessNextSequence with the signatures of adm.counter.
The order values are stored as ISO text and compared in Python as dates (D) or timestamps (DH, DHZ), so the same columns serve every dtype and every adapter.

list.item: A PostgreSQL trigger on the document table that keeps the blocks aligned on writes made outside the Python triggers (direct SQL, insertMany). Setting a number as occupied twice is harmless, so it can be added later beside the Python path.

decision.question: How are the numbers of a series kept?

option.title: holes Bag in adm.counter, as today
Contiguous blocks, occupied and free, each with first and last number and first and last order value

decision.question: Which value must the numbers follow?

option.title: order_field, optional; its dtype decides date or full timestamp; missing means no check

decision.question: Can a counter recycle without an order?
Python triggers or a PostgreSQL trigger?

option.title: PostgreSQL trigger on the document table
A new adm table, one row per block, linked to the adm.counter record of its series
A new column of adm.counter holding the blocks of its series

decision.question: Name of the table of blocks?
Name and shape of the experimental switch?

option.title: experimentalValue('db', 'counters_n') with a list of counters
experimentalValue('new_counters', 'counters'): '*' for every counter, or a list of pkg.table.field

list.item: The free numbers and their windows come from the blocks: no LIKE search, no query on the document table except at the two new edges of a release inside an occupied block.
The number is read from the blocks, not parsed back from the formatted string.
A counter with date_field and no order_field loses the date check when it moves to the new model: the switch step declares order_field where the order is required.
Writes that skip the Python triggers can still make the blocks drift, as they do with holes today.
